newsitem.title: NORWAY: Orkla income up on branded goods, stocks.
newsitem.headline: Orkla income up on branded goods, stocks.

text.p: Norwegian industrial conglomerate Orkla ASA said on Friday its 1996 profits before tax rose 29 percent because of gains in branded goods and the investment portfolio.
Pre-tax profits jumped to 2.43 billion crowns from 1.90 billion while earnings per share rose 22 percent to 36.50 crowns. The board proposed to raise the dividend to seven crowns from six crowns.
"This increase in profits is attributable to the positive performance of both the Financial Investments and the Branded Consumer Goods areas," a statement said.
The chemicals division's operating profits dropped to 441 million crowns from 543 million partly because of falling speciality pulp prices.

Group operating revenues increased by four billion crowns to about 26 billion. Operating profits rose to 1.92 billion crowns from 1.80 billion. Net profits came to 1.75 billion, up from 1.43 billion in 1995.
Operating parameters for the group's Branded Consumer Goods business in the Nordic markets were expected to remain unchanged on the whole.
Demand for speciality pulp is satisfactory but prices remain low. Fine Chemicals is expecting lower profits in 1997, Orkla said.
